newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian gunman laughed during slaughter. [CORRECTED 06:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Australian gunman laughed during slaughter. [CORRECTED 06:15 GMT]

text.p: Australian mass murderer Martin Bryant laughed as he gunned down 35 people at Port Arthur, shooting many in the head as they ate lunch and others as they pleaded for mercy, a court was told on Tuesday.

It took a mere 15 seconds for Bryant, armed with a semi-automatic rifle, to slaughter 12 people in the Broad Arrow Cafe at Port Arthur, Prosecutor Damian Bugg told the Tasmanian Supreme Court. A total of 20 people died in the cafe. (Corrects number of dead from 24).
"It's more appropriate to term what he did in that cafe as slaughter," said Bugg in a pre-sentence hearing in which he asked the judge to jail Bryant for life without parole.
Bryant has confessed to murdering 35 people at Port Arthur on April 28 and numerous attempted murder charges.
Survivors have said Bryant laughed as he killed.

"Bryant was not saying anything, but he appeared to be laughing in an aggressive way, rather than in an amused way," said Bugg, quoting the unnamed survivor. "He said Bryant walked from table to table shooting people in the head."
Bugg said Bryant told people only hours before the massacre that he intended to kill Wasps -- white, Anglo-Saxon protestants.
The first to die in Bryant's murderous spree were the owners of a guesthouse near Port Arthur, but their charred bodies were only found a day later in the burnt-out remains of the cottage.

The first to die in the cafe were Malaysian tourists Moh Yee William Ng and Sou Leng Chung. "Police investigators who attended the scene later were to observe that Mr Ng still had a dinner knife in his hand," Bugg said.

One survivor said victim Anthony Nightingale cried out: "No, no, not here", before Bryant turned on him and shot him in the neck. Another victim was heard to say "that's not funny" before being shot dead.

Bryant fired only 29 shots from a semi-autmatic rifle, but many of the 60 people crowded in the cafe were hit with flying shrapnel. "There's no doubt at his intent or his desire to cause maximum carnage," Bugg said.
Bugg said Bryant had planned his massacre for months, hiding guns in a piano in his Hobart home and making inquiries about purchasing guns months before the masscare.
"Clearly at that particular time he intended...to embark upon his murderous and violent conduct at Port Arthur," he said.

Shortly before the massacre Bryant bought a semi-automatic rifle and a semi-automatic shotgun -- the two weapons used in the shooting spree, he said. Bryant took handcuffs, rope and a hunting knife to Port Arthur, along with the two weapons and a large amount of ammunution.
The massacre had an "air of pre-planning", Bugg said.
But Bryant gave no clue to his murderous intentions the night before the massacre when he had dinner with his mother and girlfriend in Hobart, Bugg said.
On the morning of the massacre as Bryant drove from Hobart to Port Arthur, a one-hour trip, he stopped and spoke to several people at a shop and petrol station.
At one point Bryant was asked by two people whether he was going surfing, as he had a surfboard tied onto the roof of his yellow Volvo.
"No, I am going to the island of the dead to get rid of some Wasps", said Bugg, quoting the people Bryant met.
The Isle of the Dead is a small island just off Port Arthur where colonial-era convicts were buried en masse in dozens of unmarked graves.
